key_insight: Standard RL fine-tuning for LLMs collapses into a few dominant reasoning patterns because rewards focus on local token behavior; rewarding uniqueness at the solution-set level encourages diverse, creative rollouts and improves multi-sample metrics (e.g., pass@k).
problem_solved: Addresses exploration collapse in RL-finetuned LLMs where policies over-concentrate on high-probability, repetitive reasoning traces, limiting rollout-level diversity and gains from sampling multiple outputs.
method: Define a set-level uniqueness (novelty) score over model rollouts (e.g., inverse-density, clustering-distance, or rarity of reasoning traces) rather than only token-level regularizers.
Augment the RL reward with a uniqueness-aware term that upweights rare but valid solutions, balancing quality and novelty during policy optimization.
Optimize the combined objective so the model preserves correctness while producing a wider, more creative distribution of solutions (improved pass@k and exploration).
impact: Enables RL-finetuned LLMs to generate more diverse, creative solutions without sacrificing accuracy, improving effectiveness in creative problem solving, multi-sample evaluation, and downstream tasks that benefit from heterogeneous outputs.

paper_title: Rewarding the Rare: Uniqueness-Aware RL for Creative Problem Solving in LLMs
paper_authors: Zhiyuan Hu, Yucheng Wang, Yufei He, Jiaying Wu, Yilun Zhao
